entry.idea: Factory data about parts, designs and costs is scattered across many systems and paper, so CADDi builds an AI platform that pulls it all together into one place manufacturers can search and use.
entry.lesson: When an entire industry's most valuable information is trapped in messy, specialized formats, building the AI that can finally read and organize it is a huge opportunity.
entry.name: CADDi

growth.reason: Headcount grew fast, the valuation jumped from a $38M raise in 2025 to a $1.2B valuation with a $114M Series D in 2026, and it now serves manufacturers in 22 countries.

market.reason: Every manufacturer in the world deals with scattered technical and operational data, so the potential market spans a huge global industry.

tech.reason: Its ability to interpret complex, manufacturing-specific data like technical drawings is a real technical edge that would take a strong team real time to match.

entry.twist: It reads and understands messy, manufacturing-specific data, like technical drawings, that general-purpose AI tools cannot make sense of.
entry.who_pays: Manufacturers, including large automakers and industrial equipment makers, pay to use the platform to speed up design, procurement and production work.
entry.why_now: AI is now good enough to read and structure messy technical data, and manufacturers are under pressure to cut costs and delays, so there is new demand for tools that turn scattered factory data into something useful.
